definitions.explanation: To run in various directions, typically with high energy, often used for children or animals.

definitions.gloss: to rush about, to run around busily
definitions.explanation: To be very busy running from place to place to get things done.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている。
{子供|こども}たちが{庭|にわ}を{走|はし}り{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: The children ran around the yard.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{家|いえ}の{中|なか}を{元気|げんき}に{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: The cat is energetically running around inside the house.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{公園|こうえん}で{朝|あさ}から{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っていた。
examples.english: The children had been running around in the park since morning.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さな{男|おとこ}の{子|こ}が{広|ひろ}い{芝生|しばふ}の{上|うえ}を{楽|たの}しそうに{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っていた。
examples.english: A little boy was happily running around on the wide lawn.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{忙|いそが}しく{走|はし}り{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: I was busy rushing about today.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}で{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っていた。
examples.english: I was running around all day for work.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物|もの}であちこち{走|はし}り{回|まわ}らなければならなかった。
examples.english: I had to rush around from place to place for shopping.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{準備|じゅんび}のために{朝|あさ}から{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: I have been rushing about since morning to prepare for the meeting.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{手続|てつづ}きで{市役所|しやくしょ}と{銀行|ぎんこう}を{走|はし}り{回|まわ}らなければならなかった。
examples.english: I had to rush around between city hall and the bank for the moving paperwork.

notes:
{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}) meaning to run around.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {走|はし}る (to run) + {回|まわ}る (to go around) → to run around

ASPECT (ている):
{走|はし}り{回|まわ}っている indicates an ongoing action of running around, often with energy.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {元気|げんき}に{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around energetically)
- あちこち{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around everywhere)
- {忙|いそが}しく{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around busily)

USAGE NOTE:
Often used for children playing or animals being active. Also used figuratively to describe being very busy and having to go to many places.

[Register: Neutral]
